## Review: v21 selection lifetime

Read the packet in full (2693 lines). The core design — object-keyed identity records + one compaction pass, purge at every command/selection entry point plus before `Update`'s focus early-return — is sound and meets the stated requirements. `PurgeStaleSelection` (`RtsController.cs:497-530`) is linear per list, allocation-free (dictionary swap, no LINQ), and control-group recall correctly prunes by `SoldierRef.Matches`/`ShipRef.Matches` before selecting. Findings below.

### P2-1 — `RtsController.Clear()` can drop a listed live actor without deselecting it
`RtsController.cs:533-541`:
```
foreach(var unit in Selection)if(OwnsIdentity(unit))unit.Select(false);
foreach(var ship in Fleet)if(OwnsIdentity(ship))ship.Select(false);
ClearSelectionLists();
```
`Clear()` gates deselection on ownership but never purges first, so an entry present in the public list with **no** identity record is silently discarded with its ring left on. Baseline (`RtsController.cs` @@ line 176-177 of the diff) deselected every non-null entry.

Reachable exactly in the scenario this delta targets — controller disabled/unfocused, so no `Update` purge has recorded the entry:
```
controller.Selection.Add(liveUnit);   // same public-list edit as PublicListEditsAfterPoolReuseDoNotRebindTheStaleActor
controller.Clear();                   // or Escape, SelectTown(null), SelectBuildingsIn with append=false
```
`liveUnit.Selected` stays `true` while it is no longer selected; the ring persists until that actor is selected and deselected again. Note the sibling method already does it right: `RtsController.BuildingSelection.cs:1277-1282` (`ClearMobileAndCamp`) calls `PurgeStaleSelection()` before the identical `OwnsIdentity` loop — which both establishes identities for unknown live entries and drops stale ones. `Clear()` should do the same. This is a behavior regression, not a stale-actor risk: a pool-reused actor is correctly *not* deselected either way (`Soldier.Initialize` → `Select(false)`, `Soldier.cs:1874`).

### P2-2 — Regression coverage misses three behaviors the delta rewrote
`RtsSelectionLifetimeTests.cs` exercises real death → delayed `SoldierPool.Retire`/`Rent` → surviving selection → soldier group recall, with a genuine `Is.SameAs(actor)` reuse assertion (line 1595) — that part is solid. Not covered:
- **Friendly append/toggle**, which the delta rewrote from `Selection.Contains`/`Remove` to `IsSelected`/`RemoveSelected` (`RtsController.Input.cs:1131`, `RtsController.cs:553`). No test shift-clicks a selected unit or ship to deselect it, so an ownership-gate mistake there would pass.
- **Naval control-group recall**: `ShipRef`, `shipGroups[i]`, and `shipStored.RemoveAll(...)` (`RtsController.cs:926,934-938`) are never executed; `ControlGroupRecallSkipsAStoredActorThatThePoolReused` stores only soldiers, and `DestroyedShipLeavesTheFleetBeforeFleetCommandsRun` never touches groups. Land/naval grouping is an explicit requirement.
- **`Clear()`'s new ownership gate** — no test asserts `Selected` state after `Clear()`, which is why P2-1 is invisible to this suite.

### P3-1 — Duplicate stale entry swallows a deliberate re-add
`PurgeStaleSelection` line 507: an entry with a *recorded* id is dropped when the id differs. If the reused object appears twice in `Selection` (one legacy entry plus a caller intentionally re-adding the now-live rented actor, before any purge), the single map key holds the old id, so **both** occurrences are dropped and the live actor is not selected. All in-controller paths purge before adding, so this needs an external double `Selection.Add`; low reachability.

### P3-2 — Minor cost notes (no regression)
`RemoveSelected` (`RtsController.cs:485-489,559-563`) allocates a closure per call via `RemoveAll`; not on a per-frame path. `CancelBoardingForSelection` (line 619) is now an explicit nested loop, O(|Selection|×|pendingBoarders|), but `pendingBoarders` is capped at `Ship.LoadOrderLimit` (10) and the baseline `pendingBoarders.Contains(unit)` had the same complexity.

### Checked and clean
Every `Selection`/`Fleet`-reading command entry point purges: `Stop`/`Hold`/`Arm*`/`OrderAt`/`ExecuteArmedPointer`/`ContextAction`/`MoveFleetToHarbor`/`BoardNearby`/`UnloadFleet`/`Focus*`/`SelectUnits`/`SelectShips`/`SelectShip`/`SelectPrimaryUnit`. `ProcessPendingBoarding` runs before the purge in `Update` but is independently guarded by `boarder.Matches` (line 809). `BattleHud.AddSelectionCard`'s `SameLiveActor()` id capture blocks HUD clicks on a replacement (line 2604-2613). Destroyed ships fall out via the Unity-null branch of `IsSelectableShip`, consistent with ships not being pooled. No maps/rules/camera/multiplayer changes; `Selection`/`Fleet` remain plain public lists.

### Uncertainty
`BattleSession.Spawn/FindTarget/Commands.AppliedCount`, `UiViewport`, `SimClock` and `NavalWorld.Spawn` are not in the packet, so I could not verify the tests compile or that `Pump` reliably produces `wasPressedThisFrame` for the group hotkeys; per instructions I assumed nothing about execution results.

## Verdict

No provable P0/P1 correctness defect in the delta. The ownership invariant holds: after any `PurgeStaleSelection()`, `selectionIds`/`fleetIds` contain exactly the surviving list entries (the dict swap discards everything else), so `IsSelected`, `OwnsIdentity` and `AddSelected`'s `ContainsKey` guard are all consistent, and every public/HUD-callable command that reads `Selection`/`Fleet` purges first. Findings below are coverage and hygiene.

### Reachability audit (basis for "no P0/P1")
- Command entry points that submit orders or touch actors all purge before use: `Stop`, `Hold`, `ArmAttack/Move/Patrol`, `OrderAt`, `BoardNearby`, `UnloadFleet`, `MoveFleetToHarbor`, `FocusSelection`, `FocusFleet`, `ExecuteArmedPointer`, `ContextAction`, `SelectPrimaryUnit`, `SelectShip`, `SelectUnits`, `SelectShips`. `Clear`/`ClearMobileAndCamp` drop everything and deselect only owned actors, so a rented-back view keeps its own ring.
- `Update` (RtsController.cs:857) purges before the `!EffectiveFocus` and `HelpVisible/ScoreboardVisible/Winner` early returns, satisfying the "Update is skipped" requirement.
- `ProcessPendingBoarding` runs before the purge but every branch is gated on `boarder.Matches` first, with `||` short-circuit, so the re-submitted recovery `UnitCommand` at RtsController.cs:819 cannot reach a rented actor.
- Cleanup is a single stable compaction per list plus a `Dictionary.Clear`/swap — linear, no per-frame allocation.

### P1 — `pendingBoarders` identity purge is untested, though "delayed boarding orders" is an explicit requirement
`RtsController.PurgeStaleSelection` (RtsController.cs:527-529) and `ProcessPendingBoarding` (RtsController.cs:808-809) are the only code paths protecting a pool-reused view from inheriting a delayed boarding order, and `RtsSelectionLifetimeTests` has no fixture that starts a boarding (`BeginBoarding`/`BoardNearby`) at all. The reachable scenario the tests do not pin: select troops, right-click a Transport (`ContextAction` → `BeginBoarding`), lose focus, kill and re-rent a boarder via `KillAndReuse`, then let `ProcessPendingBoarding` reach its 1 s recovery window — nothing in the suite would fail if `boarder.Matches` were removed from RtsController.cs:809 or if line 528 were dropped.

### P2 — naval control-group recall (`ShipRef.Matches`) has no coverage
`shipStored.RemoveAll(entry=>!entry.Matches)` (RtsController.cs:936) is new and unexercised. `DestroyedShipLeavesTheFleetBeforeFleetCommandsRun` covers only the `Fleet` purge, never `shipGroups`; `ControlGroupRecallSkipsAStoredActorThatThePoolReused` stores a group with no ships (`Fleet` empty), so the ship branch at RtsController.cs:934-938 never executes with a stored member. Deleting that `RemoveAll` would leave the suite green while a destroyed galley re-entered the fleet on Ctrl-recall.

### P2 — friendly append/toggle semantics changed, untested
`SelectPrimaryUnit` (RtsController.Input.cs:1131) moved from `Selection.Contains(unit)`/`Selection.Remove(unit)` to `IsSelected(unit)`/`RemoveSelected(unit)`, and `ContextAction` (RtsController.Input.cs:1176) from `Selection.Contains(ally)` to `IsSelected(ally)`. Both are equivalent only because the purge at the head of each method guarantees every listed entry owns an identity — a non-obvious invariant with no test. No fixture performs a shift-append toggle or a right-click Follow on a selected ally.

### P3 — nits
- `RemoveSelected(Soldier)` / `RemoveSelected(Ship)` (RtsController.cs:487, 561) allocate a closure per call via `RemoveAll(listed=>listed==unit)` where `Remove` would do; not on a per-frame path.
- `CancelBoardingForSelection` (RtsController.cs:619) is a nested `Selection` × `pendingBoarders` scan. Complexity is unchanged from baseline (`pendingBoarders.Contains` inside the same loop) and `pendingBoarders` is bounded by `Ship.LoadOrderLimit` = 10, so this is not a regression against the "no nested selection scans" clause, only the least tidy spot in the delta.
- `groups`/`shipGroups` retain `SoldierRef`/`ShipRef` wrappers for destroyed or recycled actors until that group is next recalled. Pre-existing in shape; bounded by 9 groups.

### Stated uncertainty
`CombatTarget.EntityId` assignment is not in the packet, so I verified only that `Soldier.Initialize` calls `session.RegisterTarget(this)` (Soldier.cs:1859) and that `KillAndReuse` asserts a changed id; I could not independently confirm that a re-registered pooled view always receives a fresh id. If it did not, every `Matches`/`OwnsIdentity` check would silently pass — that assumption is the load-bearing one for the whole design.

## Review: v0.2.1 selection lifetime (baseline 2a45dcd)

Read the packet in full (2693 lines). No P0/P1 correctness defects found: every mutation of `Selection`/`Fleet` and every command-issuing entry point purges before use, `PurgeStaleSelection` is a single stable compaction per list with no LINQ/closure allocation, and the identity maps are rebuilt from list contents only (double-buffered swap), so orphaned records cannot accumulate. Findings below.

### P2 — `Clear()` and `ClearMobileAndCamp()` are asymmetric; `Clear()` can leak a selection ring
`RtsController.cs:533` `Clear()` deselects only `if(OwnsIdentity(unit))` but, unlike `RtsController.BuildingSelection.cs:1273` `ClearMobileAndCamp()` (which calls `PurgeStaleSelection()` first, `:1279`), it never purges. An entry appended straight to the public `Selection`/`Fleet` list — which the design explicitly supports (`:479-482` comment, and `RtsSelectionLifetimeTests.PublicListEditsAfterPoolReuseDoNotRebindTheStaleActor:1662-1664` exercises exactly this) — has no id record, so `OwnsIdentity` is false and `unit.Select(false)` is skipped; `ClearSelectionLists()` then drops it. If any caller pairs `Selection.Add(u)` with `u.Select(true)`, the ring stays lit permanently after Escape/`Clear()`. Baseline deselected unconditionally (`foreach(var u in Selection)if(u)u.Select(false)`), so this is a behavioural narrowing. Reachable path: external append → `Clear()` (Escape at `:899`, `SelectCamp`, `PrimaryTap` inspect branches at Input.cs:1106-1107) with no intervening `Update`. Fix is one line: purge at the top of `Clear()`, mirroring `ClearMobileAndCamp`, which re-takes identity for unknown live entries. Uncertainty stated precisely: the packet contains no caller that does `Add` + `Select(true)`, so I cannot prove an in-tree trigger; the divergence between two otherwise identical methods is the concrete evidence.

### P2 — Named requirement "delayed boarding orders" has no test
`pendingBoarders` was converted to `List<SoldierRef>` (`:442`), with match checks at `ProcessPendingBoarding:808-809`, `CancelBoardingForSelection:619` and the purge tail `:527-529`. No fixture in `RtsSelectionLifetimeTests.cs` starts a boarding (`BeginBoarding`/`BoardNearby`), kills a pending boarder, returns it through the pool, and asserts the rented-back actor is neither re-issued the landing `Move` at `:819` nor embarked by `TryEmbark` at `:809`. That is the one scenario in the requirements where a stale entry survives across many frames by design (the boarding loop is driven from `Update` *before* the purge, `:859-863`), and it is the only converted data structure with zero coverage. Regression here would be silent.

### P2 — Naval control groups are untested
`shipGroups` was converted to `List<ShipRef>` with `RemoveAll(entry=>!entry.Matches)` and `SelectShips(...,true)` at `:934-938`. `ControlGroupRecallSkipsAStoredActorThatThePoolReused:1679` only stores/recalls soldiers; `DestroyedShipLeavesTheFleetBeforeFleetCommandsRun:1711` never touches groups. Land/naval grouping and "valid group recall" are explicit requirements; the ship half of the recall path (including the append semantics that keep recalled ships additive to recalled units) has no assertion.

### P3 — Friendly append/toggle not covered after the `Contains`→`IsSelected` swap
`SelectPrimaryUnit:1131` and `SelectShip:553` changed toggle-off from `Selection.Contains(unit)`/`Fleet.Contains(ship)` to `IsSelected(...)`, which now additionally requires an id record. Correct as written (both call `PurgeStaleSelection()` first, which records unknown live entries), but no test shift-clicks a selected unit/ship to deselect it, so a future change that drops either purge would silently break shift-toggle.

### P3 — Minor, non-blocking
- `CancelBoardingForSelection:619` is a nested `Selection × pendingBoarders` scan. Bounded by `Ship.LoadOrderLimit=10` and identical in complexity to the baseline `pendingBoarders.Contains(unit)`, so not a regression, but it is the only remaining nested selection scan.
- `RemoveSelected` (`:485`, `:559`) uses `RemoveAll` with a capturing lambda — one delegate allocation per call. Not per-frame (only toggle-off paths), but `Selection.Remove(unit)` plus map removal would be allocation-free.
- Post-purge, the `OwnsIdentity` guards in `ClearMobileAndCamp:1280-1281` are always true and are dead weight; harmless, but they obscure that `Clear()`'s identical-looking guards are *not* redundant (see P2 above).

Not assessed: callers of `RtsController.Selection`/`Fleet` outside the five files in the packet (only `BattleHud.Selection.cs` is included; its card click path is correctly guarded by `SameLiveActor()` at `:2604`/`:2610`). Tests were not executed.

Read the full follow-up delta (679 lines) including the added `BattleSession`/`CombatTarget`/`SimClock` dependencies.

## Reconciliation of my original findings

**P2-1 (`Clear()` dropped an externally-listed live actor without clearing its ring) — fixed.** `RtsController.cs` `Clear()` now calls `PurgeStaleSelection()` first, then deselects every surviving entry unconditionally (delta lines 57-59); `ClearMobileAndCamp` was aligned the same way (delta lines 84-88). The gating is now in the right place: purge drops replaced actors (id mismatch, `continue` without touching `Select`) and records an identity for unknown-but-live externally listed entries, so exactly the owned set is released. The unconditional `unit.Select(false)` loops are null-safe because purge's new `if(!unit)continue` removes destroyed entries in the same call. `ClearReleasesAnExternallyListedActorButNotAReplacedOne` covers precisely this (`troops[1].Selected` false, `reused.Selected` false, and the replaced actor still ordinary-selectable afterwards).

**P2-2 (coverage gaps) — closed.** `FriendlyAppendToggleTracksIdentityAcrossPoolReuse` drives the real `SelectPrimaryUnit` (reflection on the private method, not an id swap) and asserts a stale entry cannot turn an append into a deselect. `NavalGroupRecallAndAppendToggleFollowShipIdentity` finally exercises `ShipRef`/`shipGroups` pruning plus ship append/toggle. `ClearReleasesAnExternallyListedActorButNotAReplacedOne` covers the `Clear()` gate. The two new boarding fixtures (`PendingBoardingDropsAReusedBoarderInsteadOfLandingOrLoadingIt`, `EmbarkedSelectedActorIsReleasedFromTheSelection`) exercise real `BeginBoarding`/`TryEmbark` with `Commands.AppliedCount`/`RejectedCount` held constant — genuine assertions, not reflection id swaps.

**P3-1 (duplicate stale entry) — unchanged, still open.** `PurgeStaleSelection` keys the identity map by object, so if the same reused object appears twice in `Selection` (a legacy entry plus an external re-add of the now-live rented actor before any purge), the single key holds the old id and both occurrences are dropped. Needs an external double `Selection.Add`; every in-controller path purges before adding. No test covers it. Still P3.

## Remaining findings

**P3-2 (new, minor) — purge writes to actors it does not own.** `PurgeStaleSelection` line 22/37: an entry with *no* prior record establishes `id=unit.EntityId`, so if it is also unselectable it takes the `unit.Select(false)` branch. That deselects an actor this controller never selected (external `Selection.Add` of a dead/embarked/agent-disabled soldier). Harmless in practice — every path that makes a soldier unselectable (`Soldier.TakeDamage`, `Ship.TryEmbark`, `Soldier.Initialize`) already calls `Select(false)` — so I found no reachable state where the ring is actually on. Noted for completeness only.

**No P0/P1/P2 remaining.** Requirements still hold: purge stays one linear compaction pass per list with the dictionary swap and no LINQ/allocation; `Selection`/`Fleet` remain plain public lists; pooled-rent identity comes from `CombatTarget.EntityId` re-issued in `BattleSession.RegisterTarget` (line 467-468), which confirms the reuse assumption the design rests on; ships still `Destroy` and fall out via the Unity-null branch.

## Honest limits

55/55 passing is evidence only for the assertions written. Two caveats: `reused.Selected` being false after `Clear()` is satisfied by `Soldier.Initialize`'s own `Select(false)`, not by `Clear()`, so that assertion would not detect a regression in the drop path; and the duplicate-entry case above is unasserted. `BattleCommands`, `NavalWorld.Spawn`, `Harbor`, `UiViewport` and `RiskBootstrap` are still outside the packet, so I verified test intent, not their runtime preconditions.

## Reconciliation

All three coverage gaps from my first review are now closed by fixtures that drive the real paths, not reflection-swapped ids:

- **P1 (boarding)** → `PendingBoardingDropsAReusedBoarderInsteadOfLandingOrLoadingIt` runs a real `BeginBoarding(Ship)` (private, invoked via reflection but with real actors), asserts a landing order was actually queued, then kills/re-rents through `KillAndReuse` and pumps six stall-recovery cycles. It pins the things that matter: `CargoCount == 0`, `AppliedCount`/`RejectedCount` unchanged, `replacement.IsIdle`, and the "Embarque terminado" resolution. Removing `boarder.Matches` from `ProcessPendingBoarding` or line 528 of the purge would now fail this.
- **P2 (naval group recall)** → `NavalGroupRecallAndAppendToggleFollowShipIdentity` stores a real Ctrl-group with two ships, destroys the galley, yields a frame so `Destroy` lands, and recalls. `ShipRef.Matches` is genuinely exercised.
- **P2 (append/toggle)** → `FriendlyAppendToggleTracksIdentityAcrossPoolReuse` and the ship half of the naval test cover both `IsSelected`/`RemoveSelected` toggle paths, including that a stale entry does not turn an append into a deselection.

## Review of the new code

The purge reorder is correct and closes a hole I did not raise. Splitting the two drop reasons — `unit.EntityId != id` (replaced: drop silently, its state is not ours) before `!IsSelectableSoldier(unit)` (same actor left play: `Select(false)`, then drop) — is the right precedence. A replaced view can never have its ring cleared by the old owner, and an actor that dies or embarks no longer leaks a ring.

`Clear()`/`ClearMobileAndCamp()` purging first and then deselecting unconditionally is safe: after the purge every remaining entry is non-null and owned, so the unguarded `unit.Select(false)` cannot NRE. It also fixes a real prior asymmetry — an actor appended straight to the public `Selection` list previously kept its ring through `Clear()` because `OwnsIdentity` was false. `ClearReleasesAnExternallyListedActorButNotAReplacedOne` asserts exactly that, and additionally that the replaced actor stays an ordinary selectable unit afterwards (`SelectOnly(reused)` → `Hold()` → `AppliedCount+1`).

`CombatTarget.EntityId` is now visible: `RegisterTarget` assigns `++nextEntityId` whenever the id is 0 or the entity table no longer maps that id to this object, and `UnregisterTarget` removes the id on death. Since `Soldier.TakeDamage` unregisters before the pool retire and `Initialize` re-registers, a rented view always receives a fresh monotonic id. This confirms the load-bearing assumption I flagged as unverified; it is no longer an open risk.

## Remaining

**Clean.** No P0/P1/P2 remaining.

**P3 (nit, unchanged):** `RemoveSelected(Soldier/Ship)` still allocates a predicate closure via `RemoveAll(listed=>listed==unit)` where `Remove` suffices; not on a per-frame path. `Clear()` now purges and is itself called from `SelectUnits`/`SelectShips`/`SelectShip` after those already purged, so a selection change makes two linear passes — still allocation-free and linear.

## Honest limits

- The 55/55 result is evidence only for the assertions above; I take the noted first-attempt CS1503 compile failure at face value and read the constraint changes (`Does.Contain` → `Has.Member`) as the fix, which is a test-only change.
- `StrategicMapView` is not in either packet. If it deactivates tactical actors, the new `Select(false)` branch fires on map entry. Dropping them from the list was already the baseline behavior, so this is not a regression against the reviewed delta, but I could not verify the ring behavior on returning to the tactical view.

Read the follow-up delta in full (679 lines), including the added `BattleSession`/`CombatTarget`/`SimClock` dependencies.

## Reconciliation of my original findings

- **P2 `Clear()` asymmetry — fixed.** `RtsController.Clear()` now calls `PurgeStaleSelection()` first and then deselects every surviving entry unconditionally (`:57-59`). Purge guarantees survivors are non-null (`if(!unit)continue`, `:15`) and identity-owned, so the unguarded `unit.Select(false)` cannot NRE and cannot touch a replaced actor. `ClearMobileAndCamp` was aligned identically (`:84-88`). `ClearReleasesAnExternallyListedActorButNotAReplacedOne` asserts exactly the two halves I raised: `troops[1].Selected==false` after an external `Selection.Add` + `Clear()`, and `reused.Selected==false` for the pool-replaced entry, plus that the replacement is afterwards an ordinary selectable unit (`AppliedCount==applied+1`, `reused.IsHolding`).
- **P2 boarding coverage — closed.** `PendingBoardingDropsAReusedBoarderInsteadOfLandingOrLoadingIt` drives the real `BeginBoarding(Ship)` entry, kills and re-rents the boarder while unfocused, then pumps six real boarding cadences and asserts `CargoCount==0`, `replacement.IsIdle`, and both `AppliedCount`/`RejectedCount` unchanged — i.e. neither the landing `Move` nor the stall-recovery re-issue reaches the replacement, and the queue resolves ("Embarque terminado") rather than stalling.
- **P2 naval groups — closed.** `NavalGroupRecallAndAppendToggleFollowShipIdentity` stores a mixed group via real `Ctrl+1`, exercises `SelectShip` append-toggle both ways, destroys the galley, and recalls. Note the recall reaches `shipGroups` only because `groups[i]` is also written (empty list) on store; that gating (`groups.TryGetValue` wrapping the ship branch) is unchanged from baseline and the test does cover it.
- **P3 append/toggle — closed** by `FriendlyAppendToggleTracksIdentityAcrossPoolReuse`, including the key case that a stale entry must not turn an append into a deselection.

## Remaining findings

**P3 — the new `Select(false)` in `PurgeStaleSelection` is near-unreachable for ships.** `Ship.TakeDamage` ends in `Destroy(gameObject)`, so a dead ship fails `if(!ship)continue` (`:34`) and never reaches `ship.Select(false)` (`:37`). It is reachable only for a still-live object that is deactivated or changes team. Harmless, but the ship branch carries no covering assertion; `DestroyedShipLeavesTheFleetBeforeFleetCommandsRun` exits through the null path.

**P3 — `EmbarkedSelectedActorIsReleasedFromTheSelection` is weak evidence for the new deselect path.** `Ship.TryEmbark` already calls `soldier.Select(false)` before deactivating, so `passenger.Selected==false` would hold with or without line `:22`. The list-membership half of that test is meaningful; the ring half is not.

**P3 — double purge per selection operation.** `SelectUnits`/`SelectShips`/`SelectShip` purge and then call `Clear()`, which now purges again. Both passes are O(n) and allocation-free (dictionary double-buffer, `RemoveRange`), so this is redundancy, not a per-frame cost.

No P0/P1/P2 remain in the changed code.

**Limits.** I reviewed only this delta against my prior context; the 55/55 result is evidence solely for the assertions quoted above, and the reported first-attempt `CS1503` compile failure is consistent with the `Does.Contain`→`Has.Member` constraint fixes in this delta. Callers of `Selection`/`Fleet` outside the files supplied across both packets remain unassessed.

nativeAcceptance.findings: Single portrait/stats and common Marine catalog with two five-slot queues render correctly. Fixture uses gameplay APIs and disables controller Update; it is not physical-input or pooled-focus acceptance.

webAcceptance.input: Synthetic browser CDP; ordinary paid recruitment; no injected Unity state
webAcceptance.firstPass: Completed 20 captures. Two archers selected by touch and pen; portrait card isolates one; double tap and two-contact tap move both; pen barrel starts both, one survivor remains in final capture. Desktop card and group recall were not established in this pass.
webAcceptance.followup: Completed 11 captures with key overlap spanning frames and 200ms touch contact. Desktop touch and mouse card each isolate one; group recall restores two after clear and after card selection. Two remain visible after switching browser pages; this does not establish OS focus loss or pool reuse.
webAcceptance.limits: Timing adjusted only in followup harness. No proof that all short physical taps succeed; no new runtime fix or performance certification.
